knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

## 1. Introduction

Analysis of data from a randomized controlled trial of Primary Biliary Cirrhosis (PBC).
This analysis compares the survival of patients receiving D-penicillamine (n=158) versus placebo (n=154).

## 2. Baseline Characteristics (Table 1)


```{r table1}
library(survival)
library(tableone)

data(pbc)

vars <- c("age", "sex", "ascites", "hepato", "spiders", 
          "bili", "chol", "albumin", "copper", "platelet", "stage")
catvars <- c("sex", "ascites", "hepato", "spiders", "stage")

tab1 <- CreateTableOne(vars=vars, strata="trt", 
                       data=pbc, factorVars=catvars)
print(tab1, nonnormal=c("bili","chol","copper"), showAllLevels=FALSE)
```

**Conclusion:** The groups are generally well-balanced. A significant imbalance in age was identified (p = 0.018), which was subsequently included as a covariate in the main model.

## 3. Survival Analysis — Kaplan-Meier Curves

```{r km, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
library(survminer)

fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status==2) ~ trt, data=pbc)

ggsurvplot(fit, data=pbc,
           pval=TRUE, conf.int=TRUE, risk.table=TRUE,
           legend.labs=c("D-penicillamine","Плацебо"),
           xlab="Время (дни)", ylab="Вероятность выживания",
           title="Выживаемость по группам лечения (PBC)")
```

```{r logrank}
survdiff(Surv(time, status==2) ~ trt, data=pbc)
```

**Conclusion:** No statistically significant differences in survival were observed between the treatment groups (log-rank p = 0.75).

## 4. Multivariable Cox Regression

```{r cox}
pbc$log_bili <- log(pbc$bili)

cox_final <- coxph(Surv(time, status==2) ~ trt + age + log_bili + 
                   albumin + strata(stage), data=pbc)
summary(cox_final)
```

```{r zph}
cox.zph(cox_final)
```

**Conclusion:** The proportional hazards assumption is met for all variables (global p = 0.81). D-penicillamine is not associated with improved survival after adjusting for clinical factors (HR = 1.19, 95% CI [0.82, 1.71], p = 0.365). Log-transformed bilirubin is the strongest predictor of mortality (HR = 2.60, p < 0.001).

## 5. Final Conclusion

D-penicillamine showed no survival benefit over placebo in patients with PBC. The main prognostic factors for mortality are bilirubin levels, albumin, age, and disease stage.

## 6. Logistic Regression (Secondary Analysis)

```{r logistic}
pbc$died <- as.integer(pbc$status == 2)

log2 <- glm(died ~ trt + age + log_bili + albumin + stage,
            data = pbc, family = binomial)

exp(cbind(OR = coef(log2), confint(log2)))
```
